pr.title: coverage: Store coverage source regions as `Span` until codegen (take 2)
pr.description:
This is an attempt to re-land #133418:

> Historically, coverage spans were converted into line/column coordinates during the MIR instrumentation pass.

> This PR moves that conversion step into codegen, so that coverage spans spend most of their time stored as Span instead.

> In addition to being conceptually nicer, this also reduces the size of coverage mappings in MIR, because Span is smaller than 4x u32.

That PR was reverted by #133608, because in some circumstances not covered by our test suite we were emitting coverage metadata that was causing `llvm-cov` to exit with an error (#133606).

---

The implementation here is *mostly* the same, but adapted for subsequent changes in the relevant code (e.g. #134163).

I believe that the changes in #134163 should be sufficient to prevent the problem that required the original PR to be reverted. But I haven't been able to reproduce the original breakage in a regression test, and the `llvm-cov` error message is extremely unhelpful, so I can't completely rule out the possibility of this breaking again.

r? jieyouxu (reviewer of the original PR)
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Re-landed coverage optimization that keeps coverage regions as `Span` through MIR and defers line/column conversion to LLVM codegen. The reusable correctness lesson is that this deferred conversion can reject spans (empty/improper/zero/high-bit `end_col`), and a used function may consequently have zero regions; codegen must skip such functions instead of asserting or emitting metadata that makes `llvm-cov` abort. Regression coverage uses a testing-only `-Zcoverage-options=discard-all-spans-in-codegen` flag plus an aux crate providing valid coverage metadata.
analysis.originalLogic: Historically, `InstrumentCoverage`'s `create_mappings` eagerly converted every extracted coverage span into a `SourceRegion` containing `start_line`, `start_col`, `end_line`, and `end_col`, using `make_source_region`/`ensure_non_empty_span`/`check_source_region`, and stored that 4x-u32 value in `FunctionCoverageInfo`. The PR description says: "Historically, coverage spans were converted into line/column coordinates during the MIR instrumentation pass." Codegen merely consumed the already-converted `source_region`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The reverted deferred-conversion implementation (and the naive version of this transformation) moved span-to-coordinate conversion into codegen but still assumed that a used coverage function would always end up with at least one valid region. When codegen rejected all of a function's spans, it either hit `bug!("a used function should have had coverage mapping data but did not: {covfun:?}")` or emitted coverage metadata that `llvm-cov` rejected; the PR says it was reverted because "we were emitting coverage metadata that was causing `llvm-cov` to exit with an error (#133606)." The corrected transformation skips rejected spans and returns `None` when a function has no remaining regions: `debug!(?covfun, "function has no mappings to embed; skipping"); return None;`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with coverage instrumentation, especially mappings whose spans are empty (for example, closing-brace/zero-length spans), come from macros/expansions, or are in doctests. The transformation is relevant when `InstrumentCoverage` creates mappings, when those mappings survive later MIR passes such as `CleanupPostBorrowck`, and when LLVM codegen converts the stored `Span`s into coverage coordinates. The input domain is not ordinary non-coverage Rust code; it is coverage-instrumented code where some or all mappings can be rejected by the codegen-side validation.
analysis.trigger: A coverage-instrumented function has mappings whose `Span`s cannot be converted to valid LLVM coordinates, or all of its spans are discarded during codegen (empty span not expandable to an adjacent `{`/`}`, zero line/column, `end_col` high bit set, or end before start). The regression trigger is explicitly forced with `-Zcoverage-options=discard-all-spans-in-codegen`, which makes codegen discard every span as though invalid.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and `InstrumentCoverage` has produced `Mapping { kind, span }` entries.
The deferred conversion runs during LLVM codegen rather than during MIR instrumentation.
For the all-discarded case, every mapping of a used function is rejected, leaving the function with no code/branch/MCDC regions.
The test binary still has at least one function with ordinary coverage metadata; otherwise `llvm-cov` itself complains about the absence of any coverage metadata.
pitfalls: Do not emit a coverage region when validation fails: line/column must be nonzero, `end_col`'s high bit must be unset, and `(start_line, start_col) <= (end_line, end_col)`; otherwise `llvm-cov` may exit fatally.
A used function is allowed to have no regions after codegen-side discarding; `prepare_covfun_record` must return `None` gracefully instead of retaining the old `bug!` assertion.
Empty spans are not simply passed through: `ensure_non_empty_span` tries to expand them to a neighboring `{` or `}`, but only within the function body span.

The `BytePos(1)` adjustment used for empty-span expansion is safe only because the code checks for the specific ASCII characters `{` and `}`; do not generalize it to arbitrary characters or multi-byte code points.

Moving conversion to codegen changes the MIR pretty-print representation from line/column numbers to `Span` text; test expectations must be updated, and apparent coordinate changes such as `20:1 - 20:2` becoming `20:2 - 20:2` reflect the stored empty span at MIR-dump time, not necessarily final codegen coordinates.
Doctest line numbers are adjusted in codegen, but columns are not (`FIXME(#79417)`).
The regression cannot rely on ordinary source alone; the test uses an auxiliary crate so the test binary retains valid coverage metadata while the main crate's spans are all deliberately discarded.
analysis.testStrategy: Inspect the changed `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.InstrumentCoverage.diff` and `*.CleanupPostBorrowck.diff` expectations to verify that coverage mappings are now printed as `Span` values (for example `$DIR/instrument_coverage.rs:10:1: 10:11 (#0)`) rather than `line:col - line:col`, while keeping the same counter/expression assignments. Add the regression test `tests/coverage/discard-all-issue-133606.rs` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcoverage-options=discard-all-spans-in-codegen`, an `//@ aux-build: discard_all_helper.rs`, and a call to `discard_all_helper::external_function()`, so the main crate discards all spans but the linked auxiliary crate supplies normal coverage metadata. Then run the coverage test harness to check that codegen emits no invalid metadata and `llvm-cov` does not fail. Also keep tests for empty spans and brace expansion, since those exercise `ensure_non_empty_span`. No compiler was built and no execution was performed here; this strategy is derived from the supplied patch and its test changes.
evidence: +        debug!(?covfun, "function has no mappings to embed; skipping");
